name: Our Lady of Lourdes Shrine and Divine Mercy Retreat Center

name: Mawanella Rajamaha Viharaya
description: Mawanella Rajamaha Viharaya, a sacred Buddhist temple nestled in the serene hills of Kegalle district, stands as a testament to ancient artistry and spiritual devotion. historical_significance: Mawanella Rajamaha Viharaya, located in Mawanella, is a notable example of a Tempita Vihara. Constructed on raised stone pillars, it exemplifies the architectural design of these unique Buddhist shrines. Built in 1755 by Kirti Sri Rajasinha, it was originally a two-story structure but was transformed into a Tempita Vihara. This site, along with Minuwangamuwa Tempita Vihara, represents the last Tempita Viharas built in Sri Lanka, highlighting the importance of these structures in Buddhist architecture.

historical_significance: Warakapola Rajamaha Viharaya, located in the North Western province, is a unique Tempita Vihara. name: Galigamuwa Rajamaha Viharaya
description: Discover the ancient splendor of Galigamuwa Rajamaha Viharaya, a sacred Buddhist temple nestled amidst lush paddy fields. Built over 1,500 years ago, this site houses intricate carvings and statues that narrate tales of Buddha's life. Its serene atmosphere and historical significance make it a must-visit for both locals and tourists alike.
activities: Explore ancient carvings, Learn about Buddhist history, Relax in the serene surroundings
historical_significance: Galigamuwa Rajamaha Viharaya, identified as one of the more than two hundred Tempita Viharas in Sri Lanka, stands out due to its architectural uniqueness. Constructed in the 17th to 19th centuries, it exemplifies the popular aspect of Buddhist temples during that era. The Tempita Vihara, perched on raised stone pillars, features wooden platforms and wattle walls supporting a timber-framed roof. Its design includes exposed pillars, inner walls adorned with murals, and a two-pitched roof covered with clay tiles. Over time, additional features like a wall surrounding the ground floor and a dancing hall were added, enhancing its utility and cultural significance.

name: Gammannagoda Tampita Viharaya
description: Gammannagoda Tampita Viharaya is a sacred Buddhist temple situated in the picturesque Kegalle district of Sri Lanka’s Sabaragamuwa Province. This ancient temple complex dates back to the 12th century and is renowned for its unique rock-cut cave shrines known as ‘tampita viharas’. The temple is perched on a hill, offering visitors a breathtaking view of the surrounding countryside. Visitors can explore the intricate carvings and paintings inside the cave shrines, which depict various Buddhist deities and scenes from the Jataka tales. The temple also houses several Buddha statues and other religious artifacts, providing a glimpse into the rich cultural and spiritual heritage of Sri Lanka. The serene atmosphere and the architectural beauty of the tampita viharas make Gammannagoda Tampita Viharaya a must-visit for both religious pilgrims and tourists interested in Sri Lanka’s history and culture. Visitors can also take part in guided tours led by local monks who offer insights into the temple’s history and significance. While the temple itself is free to enter, donations are appreciated.
activities: Explore caves, take guided tours, meditate, learn about Buddhism

name: Lewke Tampita Viharaya
